name: COVID-19
description: An infectious respiratory disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, primarily affecting the lungs and respiratory system.

recommendations.lifestyle: Isolate from others, monitor blood oxygen saturation, rest extensively, and avoid strenuous tasks.
recommendations.diet: Consume protein-rich meals, warm liquids (e.g., broths, herbal teas), and citrus fruits for vitamin C.
recommendations.exercise: Strictly rest. Avoid exercises until fully cleared. Light stretching is acceptable if asymptomatic.
recommendations.waterIntake: Drink 3.0 to 3.5 liters of fluids daily to thin mucus and prevent dehydration.
recommendations.sleep: Aim for 9 to 10 hours of restorative sleep, using an extra pillow to elevate your head if coughing.
recommendations.followUp: Check symptoms daily. Seek immediate emergency care if chest pain or severe breathlessness develops.

name: Hypertensive Crisis
description: A severe increase in blood pressure that can lead to stroke, heart attack, or damage to blood vessels.
causes: Poor compliance with blood pressure medications

recommendations.lifestyle: Immediately sit down in a quiet, dark room. Avoid any physical activity. Measure BP again in 5 minutes.
recommendations.diet: Strict zero-sodium intake during crisis. Follow DASH diet principles (fruits, veggies, whole grains) long-term.
recommendations.exercise: No exercise during crisis. Incorporate 30 mins of moderate walking daily after medical clearance.
recommendations.waterIntake: Drink water in moderate amounts. Avoid energy drinks, coffee, tea, or alcohol.
recommendations.sleep: Ensure consistent rest. Sleep apnea management is highly recommended.
recommendations.followUp: If blood pressure remains above 180/120 mmHg, seek EMERGENCY medical attention immediately.

name: Gastroenteritis
description: An inflammation of the stomach and intestines, typically resulting from bacterial toxins or viral infection, commonly called stomach flu.

recommendations.lifestyle: Stay near restroom facilities. Practice strict hand hygiene. Avoid preparing food for others.
recommendations.diet: Follow BRAT diet (Bananas, Rice, Applesauce, Toast). Avoid dairy, high-fat, spicy, or sugary foods.
recommendations.exercise: Rest fully. Do not engage in high-intensity training. Gentle walking is okay once hydration improves.
recommendations.waterIntake: Drink Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) or electrolyte solutions. Aim for 2.5 to 3 liters of fluids.
recommendations.sleep: Get 8 to 9 hours of sleep to assist mucosal gut lining recovery.
recommendations.followUp: Consult a doctor if symptoms persist past 3 days, or if blood is present in vomit/stools.

name: Influenza (Flu)
description: A highly contagious viral infection of the respiratory passages causing fever, severe aching, and catarrh.
causes: Influenza viruses (Type A or B) spreading via airborne aerosols
Direct hand-to-face contact after surface exposure
complications: Worsening of chronic conditions like asthma

recommendations.lifestyle: Stay home from work or school. Use humidifier to ease breathing. Avoid close contact with family members.
recommendations.diet: Warm soups, herbal teas with honey, and nutrient-dense, easily digestible foods.
recommendations.exercise: Rest until fever has subsided for at least 48 hours. Resume active sports gradually.
recommendations.waterIntake: Drink at least 2.5 to 3 liters of warm water, broths, and clear juices daily.
recommendations.sleep: Ensure 9+ hours of sleep. Resting supports the immune system's antiviral response.
recommendations.followUp: Monitor fever levels. Contact a clinician for antivirals (e.g., Tamiflu) if diagnosed early.
recommendations.doctor: General Physician or Family Medicine Doctor

name: Dehydration & Heat Exhaustion
description: A condition caused by excessive loss of water and electrolytes, often exacerbated by exposure to high temperatures.
causes: Prolonged exposure to direct sunlight or hot environments

recommendations.lifestyle: Move to a cool, air-conditioned environment immediately. Loosen tight clothing and apply cool damp cloths.
recommendations.diet: Eat water-rich foods like watermelon, cucumbers, and oranges. Avoid heavy protein or hot meals.
recommendations.exercise: Completely cease physical activities. Refrain from exercising in temperatures above 85°F (29°C).
recommendations.waterIntake: Sip cool water or electrolyte-electrolyte solutions slowly. Drink 1 liter over the first hour.
recommendations.sleep: Rest in a cool room. Elevate legs slightly if dizzy.
recommendations.followUp: Seek emergency medical help if confusion, loss of consciousness, or inability to keep fluids down occurs.
